item: A refusal by the socket guard under our resolver wrapper reads as airplane mode, not as a DNS failure (R300 b)
refs: PR #1554; R300; found by the R254 read of PR #1546
summary: If the kill switch engages between the pre-fetch check and the lookup, EthicalFetcher._resolve_cached raised cannot resolve host 'h': airplane mode is engaged: ... which classify_fetch_failure read as dns (a host failure) and feed verification stored as unreachable. is_kill_switch_refusal now recognises that third shape: it must START with our resolver sentence, a host token with no whitespace and then the guard's sentence immediately, so a gaierror text between the two, a lookalike with a spaced host, or the whole wrapped text quoted inside an HTTP or redirect failure stays dns or http. Pinned by a test built from the real resolve path (guard installed, kill switch engaged, _resolve_cached called), plus rows and controls in test_fetch_verdict and test_refusal_sentence. Two mutants killed (the alternative removed; the host token loosened). The robots-read twin of this race is Export's R297 and is untouched.
